newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends session up 3/8 point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - ends session up 3/8 point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended Friday's session up 3/8 point to as much as 1/2 point in spots, as traders said unsold bonds from the week's new issues continued to hold back a stronger rally.
The Treasury market outperformed munis, as the long bond gained 20/32 at 99 to yield 6.58 percent.
"We outperformed Treasuries all week. It's their turn to catch up," one municipal trader said.
Muni gains came on the coattails of the government market, where analysts said a rising dollar was helping push bond prices higher.

In the muni secondary, bids on Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, Ill., AMBAC 5-1/4s of 2027 were one basis point lower at 5.71 percent. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were down three basis points to 5.64 percent.

Debt futures also closed with gains. The March municipal contract jumped 26/32 to 115-18/32, while March T-bonds rose 24/32 to 113-3/32. The MOB spread widened to 74 ticks from 72 at the close on Thursday.
Next week's calendar features $3.14 billion in 109 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Competitive sales total $680 million in 65 issues. The largest issue is a $130 million King County, Wash., issue on Monday. Negotiated sales total $2.46 billion in 44 offerings, topped by the New York City deal through Lehman Brothers.
